transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we proceed. Yesterday, while tracing a failed local build for an unrelated repository, I discovered that 14 legacy CI jobs use the old registry endpoint in a way that cannot follow the planned DNS redirect. The cutover will need a compatibility proxy for those 14 jobs and a 14-day overlap period. I haven't filed the migration ticket update yet, but this directly impacts the current runbook and the planned DNS switch.

I recorded the results in my infrastructure notes but haven't updated the runbook yet — so the current draft calling for four transfer workers is not viable at production volume.

Second, service-account access to the new registry must require MFA-backed workload identity, and the draft runbook includes no additional access-control change. I have not opened the security finding yet, but these are blockers for production approval per the migration approval checklist's security controls requirement.

transcript.text:
Thank you all three for flagging these issues — this is exactly why we do the pre-approval check-in. Let me make sure I have the full picture before I make any cutover decision.

Leon: 14 legacy CI jobs can't follow the DNS redirect, so we need a compatibility proxy and a 14-day overlap period. That changes the runbook fundamentally and pushes the timeline.

Iris: Four workers exceeds the storage service's safe write rate, and three workers takes six hours — which fits within our 22:00 to 02:00 window, but only barely. The current four-worker plan in the draft is not viable at production volume.

Noah: The 30-day log retention in the draft is short of the required 180-day immutable retention, and the runbook is missing the MFA-backed workload identity access-control change. Both are blockers under the migration approval checklist.

Given all three of these, I cannot approve the production cutover as currently drafted. We need updated transfer-capacity evidence with the viable three-worker configuration, the compatibility proxy and 14-day overlap plan incorporated, and the security controls — 180-day immutable retention and MFA-backed workload identity — documented in the runbook before I'll sign off. I'd like each of you to file your respective findings and update the migration ticket and runbook promptly so we can schedule a revised approval review.
